title: Migrate birth dates out of an old table

blocks.text: The loyalty system is moving customers' birth dates to a `DATE` column. The old table has three `int` columns, `year`, `month` and `day`, which a service from 2003 filled straight from `Date.getYear()`, `Date.getMonth()` and `Date.getDate()`. Some rows were typed in by hand over the years and name days that never existed; the migration must set those aside for a person to fix, not guess a date for them. The old reports keep reading the table until the switch, so new rows must still be written in the old form.

`migrate(...)` already loops over the rows. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/BirthDates.java`: `toLocalDate(...)`, from the old columns to a `LocalDate`, and `toColumns(...)`, the other way. About two lines in total.

cases.says: the columns written for a date read back as the same date
the old month column holds the month counted from zero
the old year column holds the year minus 1900
a row naming a day that does not exist is set aside, not rolled into the next month

origin.section: Months Count From 0, Years From 1900, and Out-of-Range Values Roll Over

concepts: A lenient Calendar, the default, carries out-of-range fields into the next field, so 30 February becomes 2 March instead of an error.
Calendar and the deprecated Date constructors and getters count months from 0, and Date counts years from 1900.
